messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 15:43 UTC — Canary rollout 'gw-v2' started in eu-west (10% traffic). Alert: spike in 502/503 from eu-west edge within 3m. Paging on-call.

raj (on-call): On it — looking at traces and edge logs. Notified SRE rotation.

raj (on-call): Quick triage: other regions healthy, only eu-west shows >3% 5xx. Canary weight 10% to green pool.

matt (eng-release): FYI we rolled traffic weights: blue 90 -> green 10. No schema changes, just route shift.

raj (on-call): Logs show upstream resolve failures and mixed upstream hostnames. Some requests are hitting green but getting `502` with upstream host mismatch. Suspect DNS/CNAME or edge sticky map.

leo (netops): Possible CDN sticky mappings still pointing to retired blue backends. When we flip some edges try to route to green which expects a different host header.

raj (on-call): Can we pause the rollout? Need kill-switch. Feature flag `gw_v2_enabled` controlled by rollout-service.

amanda (sre-lead): I'll take primary. Raj — handoff to me. Raj, paste anything you have (sample logs, repro). @matt stand by to flip the flag if we decide.

raj (on-call): Handoff notes: reproducible from eu-west edge nodes. curl shows 502, upstream header shows green host. Sample request/response:

```
Host: gateway.redwood-eu
X-Forwarded-For: 3.4.5.6
Status: 502
Upstream: green-01.eu-west
```
\nraj (on-call): Also seeing a subset of edges resolving CNAME -> old-blue IPs intermittently. TTLs might be long on some nodes.

matt (eng-release): Preparing kill switch. Will run `rolloutctl set-flag gw_v2_enabled false --region eu-west` on my mark.

matt (eng-release): running now.

deploy-bot: command accepted — rolloutctl set-flag gw_v2_enabled false --region eu-west (initiated by matt).

incident-bot: ACTION: Partial rollback / flag flip started. Traffic weight change request: green 10 -> 0 over next 30s.

amanda (sre-lead): While rollback occurs, purge CDN edge sticky mappings for eu-west to clear stale host->ip caches. @leo can you purge and confirm?

leo (netops): Purging edge caches now: `cdnctl purge --region eu-west --pattern "gateway*"` — started. Propagation estimated ~2 minutes.

cs-darren: CS reports two EU customers reported timeouts at ~15:45 UTC. Collecting customer IDs and impact windows.

amanda (sre-lead): Thanks Darren. Preliminary impact estimate: ~1.8% of total requests in eu-west during the spike window (15:43–15:53). No signs of data loss. CS to send templated incident note.

matt (eng-release): Rollback complete: canary stopped, route weights restored to blue 100. Deployment id abc123 reverted.

incident-bot: METRICS: 502/503 counts dropping toward baseline 4m after rollback & purge.

raj (on-call): Confirming: error rate returned to baseline across eu-west POPs. Edge error logs show resolved host headers now consistently `gateway.redwood-eu` pointing to blue backends.

amanda (sre-lead): Preliminary root cause: mismatch between new green backend's expected host header and edge cached DNS/CNAME/sticky mapping. Partial rollout exposed inconsistency on a subset of CDN edges with longer-than-expected TTLs.

amanda (sre-lead): Immediate remediation checklist: 1) Stop rollout (done). 2) Purge CDN sticky mappings (done). 3) Confirm metrics recovered (monitoring). 4) CS outreach (Darren). 5) Draft postmortem.

matt (eng-release): I'll open a PR to add a pre-rollout CDN purge step when host header or upstream host changes are included in a deployment, and gate rollouts on zero-downtime compatibility tests.

amanda (sre-lead): Also adding a canary throttling rule: if 5xx > 1% for 2m, auto-pause rollout and notify oncall.

raj (on-call): Handing back watch to me. I'll monitor for 30m and own the postmortem draft.

amanda (sre-lead): Thanks — good catch. Tagging follow-ups: @matt, @leo, @cs-darren.

matt (eng-release): ACK.

leo (netops): Confirmed CDN purge propagated to 95% of edges at +2m, 99% at +5m.

cs-darren: I'll prepare customer messages and send to affected tenant list within 30m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 15:58 UTC — Status changed to: mitigated. Owner: raj (on-call). Postmortem requested by amanda (sre-lead).

amanda (sre-lead): Adding notes: do a tighter validation of host/header matching during canary, and include CDN TTL checks in rollout readiness. Closing primary incident channel; follow-ups tracked in postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
